print_errors.note: The closing square bracket has no matching opening bracket. The only bracket pair nearby, «[اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ … وَسَلِّمْ]», is already closed on line 4, and p.076 has no unclosed «[» either. Kept as printed.

Third centered line of the Idrisi tahlil. «وَسِعهُ» has fatha on the waw, kasra under the sin and damma on the ha, but nothing on the ain. «عِلمُ» has no sukun on the lam. Checked at 2000 dpi. Kept as printed.

«كلِ» has only one kasra. It sits low, below the depth of the final lam's bowl, so it belongs to the lam rather than the kaf (2400 dpi). There is no damma on the kaf and no shadda. «في» has no kasra. Kept as printed.
Spelled with hamza above the alif (أ), not «الإدريسي». Kept as printed.

notes:
Markers: p.076 ends mid-dua with «…أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ،» and the parenthesis still open. p.077 continues it with «أَسْتَغْفِرُكَ وَأَتُوبُ إِلَيْكَ)», so it is <<<ص:077+>>>. There is no footnote on p.076 or anywhere in this batch, so there is no (تابع) and no :::حواشي. p.077 ends «…مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ» and p.078 starts «اللَّهِ ﷺ)» (078+). p.078 ends «* يَا» and p.079 starts «حَاضِرًا لَا يَغِيبُ)» (079+). p.079 ends «وَهُوَ حَسْبُنَا» and p.080 starts «وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ» (080+).

Paragraphs: every dua line that opens with «(» or «[» is first-line indented, so each starts a paragraph. Lines that start flush right are joined to the previous line as wraps. On p.078, «[تقرأ مرة واحدة للمتعجل]» stands alone on a line after the full-width «(لَا إِلَهَ … ذَنْبَنَا) (ثلاثًا).», with no indent, so it is joined to that paragraph. The «[الصافات: …]» line on p.080 is likewise joined to its Quran paragraph.

Centered verse block on p.077 (STRUCTURE calls these short centered verse lines): the first two lines are laid out in two columns with a wide hemistich gap, so they are a :::شعر fence with ' *** '. The third line is a single centered line, «وَسِعهُ عِلمُ الله [مائة مرة]», so it is a separate :::شعر مشطور fence. The block is set in a heavier face (stroke width about 17-22 px against 12-14 px in the body at 1200 dpi). Because it is a whole block in one font, it gets no ** markup, per §6. The tatweel stretching in these lines (and in «فاعْلَمْ أَنَّهُ», «إِلَهَ», «الله», «مُحَمَّدٌ», «رَسُولُ» on line 11) is dropped.

Bold: none in this batch. On p.077 and p.079 the word «مُحَمَّدٍ/مُحَمَّدٌ/مُحَمَّدًا» looks dense, but it is the font's محمد ligature. It looks identical on p.049, where it is not marked bold. The measured stroke width (2·area/perimeter at 1200 dpi) is 13.2 against 12-13.7 for the neighbouring words, so it is not bold. Note: my b19 marked «**مُحَمَّدٍ**» on p.075; this measurement suggests that may also be just the ligature, and the adjudicator may want to recheck it. Line 11 of p.077, «( لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا الله * مُحَمَّدٌ رَسُولُ الله)», measures the same as the body (12-14.7), so it is not bold.

Allah: plain «الله» where only the ligature's own shadda and small alif are drawn: p.077 l.2, l.11-12, the verse lines, and p.079 «(صلواتُ الله». The case vowel is printed in three places, and those are written in full: p.077 last line «إِلَّا اللَّهُ،» (damma over the ligature), p.078 first word «اللَّهِ ﷺ» (kasra printed low under the ha, between the lines; line 2 is indented, so nothing else is under it), and p.079 last line «بِاللَّهِ» (a second, lower kasra under the ha besides the ba's kasra). This follows the b19 handling. ﷺ on p.078 is the printed glyph and is kept.

Other checks at high zoom: «وَاحِدٌ رَّبَّنَا» (p.078) has shadda+fatha on the ra as well as on the ba (idgham after tanween; 2600 dpi), so it is written رَّبَّنَا. «وَكُن لَّنَا» has no sukun on the nun and a shadda on the lam. «الْأَبْرَارِ» has sukun on the lam, hamza+fatha on the alif, sukun on the ba and fatha on the ra (4000 dpi). «الْمَوْلَى» (p.080) has sukun on the lam, fatha on the mim and sukun on the waw (6000 dpi; the sukun and fatha overlap). «الْمُبَارَكَاتِ» (p.079) has the sukun on the lam drawn overlapping the damma of the mim. «وَعُثْمَانَ» has a fatha on the mim. «بِهِ» ×2 (p.077) has kasra on both letters. «قَرِيب» (p.078) has no mark on the final ba. «ربَّ» has shadda+fatha in the Amin lines on p.078 (lines 7, 13, 16) and p.079 (line 2); the other Amin lines have a bare «رب» (p.078 lines 4 and 10, p.079 line 5). «(ثلاثًا)» has fathatan only, every time. Lam-alif: every fatha on لا in this batch sits over the right upright (lam) stroke, checked one by one at 2000-2400 dpi, so all are written لَا / مَوْلَانَا. Final ى with the Lotus automatic small alif is written plain: عَلَى, إِلَى, مَضَى, الْمَوْلَى, على, إلى.

Quran: 37:180-182 (p.077 and again p.080), al-Fatiha 1-7 with the basmala inside the bracket as ayah (١) (as in b18), and 33:56. scripts/quran.py reports no flags. The silent alif in ءَامَنُوا۟ / صَلُّوا۟ / وَسَلِّمُوا۟ carries a printed round zero, distinct from the khaa-head sukun in تَسْلِيمًا, so it is ۟. ۚ follows ٱلنَّبِىِّ, and there is a small waw on وَمَلَٰٓئِكَتَهُۥ.

Spacing: «(فاعْلَمْ أَنَّهُ ) ( لَا» has a full word-space before the first «)» and after the second «(» (about 70 and 50 px at 1100 dpi, against about 20 px for the tight «(فا»), so these spaces are kept as printed. «].آمين» after al-Fatiha is set tight, with no space after the period, and is written so. ﴾ and [ always get a space. A space is written after the colon in every reference. «عَالِمَ الْأَسْرَارِ» and «عَالِمَ السِّرِّ» are two words: the final mim's tail runs under the next alif, but they are written with a space. Inline flower separators ❋ on p.077 and p.078 are written ' * '. Running heads, page numbers, bracket flowers and ayah ornaments are omitted, except for the digits in the ornaments.
